To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in nanostructured superstructures:

1) the shape of the critical temperature Tc(H) versus magnetic field phase boundary in a mesoscopic superconductor is determined by the sample confinement topology; 2) the confinement topology determines the lowest Landau energy ELLL; 3) ELLL is the energy of the superconductivity order parameter; and 4) the energy of the order parameter is measured in temperature units.
the Tc(H)-phase boundaries in nanostructured superstructures are determined by the topology of the confinement of the superconductive condensate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between the confinement topology and the superconducting properties of the material.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Tc(H)-phase boundaries are determined by the lowest Landau-level energies of the superconductors under study.
in all investigated nanostructured superconducting samples the confinement topology determines the Tc(H)-phase boundary.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the shape of the phase boundary Tc(H) can be used as a tool to determine the topology of a superconducting sample.
the shape of the superconductivity phase boundary in mesoscopic samples is governed by the topology of the confining potential.
the Tc(H)-curves of the nanostructured superconducting samples are the fingerprints of the confinement topology of the sample.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in nanostructured superconductor the confinement of the condensate is a crucial factor in determining the shape of the phase boundary.
in all nanostructured samples, the confinement of superconducting condensation is determined by topology.
the confinement topology is a crucial parameter that has to be taken into account when interpreting the results of the measurements of the Tc-H phase boundary in nanostructured superconductor.
